doc.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Accompanying the Nicholas Brothers' tap dancing on bass
summary: With no music for the Nicholas Brothers, Lewis matches every slide and tap on the bass.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Oh man, we get out there, now the Nicholas Brothers didn’t have any music. So they [inaudible] bass. So I created a tune to fit every tap that they made on the floor. Oh, man, it was the bass, and doing all that stuff with slides and tumbles and all those things. And so they liked it so well, they wanted to write it up. I can’t even remember what it was now. But it fit them just like it was a glove.
That’s really interesting how the dance and music are so intertwined.

So every time they’d slide, I’d make a slide on the bass. And they’d flip, when they hit they’d make little thumps, I had all kinds of tricks I could do you know. And the bass players, they are doing that stuff now you know. I was doing it way back then. Because it sounded good to me.
